headline: Record revenue and Visa gain drive a sharp profit jump
summary_short: JPMorgan Chase reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $21.2B ($7.70 diluted EPS), up 41% y/y, including $5.6B of one-time Visa and equity-investment gains; excluding those, net income was $16.9B ($6.14 EPS), with the release's own reported revenue of $57.3B (+28% y/y) and ROTCE of 29%.
summary_long: Net income of $21.2B (+41% y/y, +28% q/q) included $4.6B from the Visa share exchange and $1.0B of equity-investment gains; excluding these, net income was $16.9B and ROTCE was 23% versus a reported 29%. Reported revenue of $57.3B (+28% y/y) was led by CIB, where Markets revenue rose 35% (Equity Markets +86%) and Investment Banking fees rose 30% to the highest since 2021. CCB revenue rose 8% on wealth-management and card growth; AWM revenue rose 19% with AUM at $5.1T (+18% y/y). Expense of $27.3B (+15% y/y) tracked higher compensation and technology spend. CET1 stood at 14.1% (Standardized); the firm repurchased $6.2B of stock and paid a $1.50/share dividend. No forward guidance was issued in the release.

drivers.explanation: Included $4.6B Visa share-exchange gain and $1.0B of equity-investment gains; excluding these, net income was $16.9B, up 13% y/y ex-items per the release.
Growth was led by CIB (Markets +35%, Equity Markets +86%, IB fees +30% to the highest since 2021), plus CCB +8% and AWM +19% per segment results.
Book value per share rose 9% y/y to $133.01 under the release's Fortress Principles disclosure, consistent with retained quarterly profit.

Release attributes results to a favorable, elevated market-activity environment plus rigorous execution and consistent investment; management also flagged geopolitical tension, sticky inflation, and fiscal-deficit risk as ongoing watch items.
